definitionOfDone: The three-line phrase is spelled exactly and matches the reference line breaks, spacing rhythm, and overall width hierarchy.
Every glyph is an independent rounded padded volume with a real counter where the reference shows one.
Fabric reads as short-pile textile rather than smooth plastic under neutral and grazing light.
Seams, color-per-glyph variation, contact shadows, and action-ready pivots are present and inspectable.
Each glyph has a hybrid rigid-proxy plus soft-body response: collision impulse, squash/stretch, twist, spring recovery, and independently tunable softness/bounce.
The visible shell also carries localized vertex deformation: a bend field and front-surface dimple that follow the impact anchor instead of only scaling the whole group.
A deterministic showcase can ripple impacts through neighboring letters without merging their physics bodies.

lightingFromPhoto: Key light: broad warm source from upper camera-left, producing soft highlights on pile and darker right-side seam response.
Fill light: low-intensity warm ambient fill keeps counters readable without flattening relief.
Rim/environment light: subtle neutral lift on upper side walls separates colorful glyphs from the cream background.
Exposure and tone mapping: neutral exposure with ACES/filmic response for saturated textile colors.
Contact shadow: soft AO/contact shadow directly below and between letters grounds each independent prop.

actionReadiness.contract: Every row and glyph is a stable named Object3D pivot with a mesh child, action metadata, collider proxy, and detachable grouping.
authoringRules: Do not collapse independent glyphs into one mesh.
Put transforms on row and glyph pivots.
Use shared geometry with separate Object3D instances where performance allows.
Use compound collider proxies rather than visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Detach and animate existing glyph groups; avoid random mesh explosions.

proceduralStrategy: Use a deterministic text layout with recorded line strings and a rounded bold typeface.
Build each character as a real extruded shape with rounded bevel and actual holes for counters.
Create separate named row and glyph pivots for animation and collisions.
Add seam contours as shared curve-sweep geometry and short-pile response as independent procedural material fields.
Assign a deterministic saturated palette slot per glyph while preserving the reference sequence.
Attach a hybrid soft-body layer to each glyph: Rapier rigid proxy for collision, spring squash/stretch for visual compression, and stable base quaternions for physics-safe deformation.

Drive a GPU vertex-shell deformation field per glyph: localized bend plus front-surface dimple with deterministic origin and size uniforms, so impact reads as a real surface response rather than only a group scale.
Drive impact pulses from collision events and velocity spikes; propagate a bounded wave to nearby glyphs for readable secondary motion.
Expose per-glyph softness, bounce, squash, impact-wave and breeze controls without changing the independent root contract.
Provide a magnetic assembly controller that selects independent glyphs, flies them along staggered spring-like arcs into a word, and restores the source grid on reset.
Render with orthographic/front, 3/4, and side cameras before approving the pass.
